newsitem.title: UK: Tate & Lyle sees H1 lower, warns on stg.
newsitem.headline: Tate & Lyle sees H1 lower, warns on stg.

text.p: British sweetener and animal feed producer Tate & Lyle Plc said on Thursday it expected results for the six months to March 1997 to be below the year-earlier half but above the second half of the 1996 financial year.
The company said the strength of sterling adversely affected profit before tax for the first quarter ended December 1996 by 7.1 million stg.
It said if current exchange rates prevailed throughout the remainder of the financial year, results for the full-year would be "marginally" lower than the 1996 year.
Tate & Lyle said the currency impact resulted from the translation of foreign currencies and the Common Agricultural Policy currency mechanism.

"Excluding this currency impact, profit before tax for the quarter was, as expected, below the corresponding period last year which had benefited from good margins in maize sweeteners in the U.S.," Tate & Lyle said in the statement.

The company said the revaluation of the green pound hit results at Tate & Lyle Sugars in the first quarter. Profits were cut by 1.6 million stg. The company did not give an absolute figure for the quarter.

Tate & Lyle said results for the year in dollars at its U.S. unit Staley would be in line with its expectations because of reduced costs and a shift in production towards non-high fructose corn syrup products.

But it said favourable trends in U.S. sugar markets and reduced operating costs raised dollar profits in the group's U.S. sugar companies in the first quarter compared with the year-earlier quarter. It said the improvement would more than offset the expected downturn at Staley.
The company said profits from its sweetener and starches operations in Africa improved in the first quarter.
But lower production cut profit contributions from Australia and adverse conditions in Russia and Thailand hit results from sugar trading operations.
Tate & Lyle released the statement ahead of its annual general meeting today. The current financial year ends September 28, 1997.
